title: The derived couple of an exact couple is exact
statement: Let $(D,E,\alpha,f,g)$ be an exact couple in an abelian category [def-sp-exact-couple], with $d=g\circ f:E^{p,q}\to E^{p+2,q-1}$. Then $\ker(d)=f^{-1}(\ker g)=f^{-1}(\operatorname{im}\alpha)$ and $\operatorname{im}(d)=g(\operatorname{im}f)=g(\ker\alpha)$ (as subobjects of $E^{p,q}$); the maps $\alpha',f',g'$ of the derived couple $(D',E',\alpha',f',g')$ of [def-sp-exact-couple] ($D'^{p,q}=\operatorname{im}(\alpha:D^{p+1,q-1}\to D^{p,q})$, $E'^{p,q}=\ker d/\operatorname{im}d$) are well defined, $g'$ being the unique map with $g'\circ\bar\alpha=\pi\circ\hat g$ for the epimorphism $\bar\alpha:D^{p+1,q-1}\twoheadrightarrow D'^{p,q}$, the factorization $\hat g:D^{p+1,q-1}\to\ker d\subseteq E^{p+1,q-1}$ of $g$ and the projection $\pi:\ker d\to E'^{p+1,q-1}$; and the derived couple is again an exact couple, with $\alpha'$ of bidegree $(-1,+1)$, $f'$ of bidegree $(+2,-1)$, $g'$ of bidegree $(+1,-1)$, and at every bidegree the kernel of each of its arrows equal to the image of its predecessor. Consequently the iterated couples $C_2=(D,E,\alpha,f,g)$, $C_{r+1}=C_r'$ are exact couples for all $r\geq2$; $C_r=(D_r,E_r,\alpha_r,f_r,g_r)$ has $D_r^{p,q}=\operatorname{im}(\alpha^{r-2}:D^{p+r-2,q-r+2}\to D^{p,q})$, $\alpha_r$ the restriction of $\alpha$, $f_r$ of bidegree $(+2,-1)$, $g_r$ of bidegree $(r-2,2-r)$, and $E_{r+1}=\ker d_r/\operatorname{im}d_r$ with $d_r=g_r\circ f_r$ of bidegree $(r,1-r)$.
